The logo melts at the speed you scroll

Nothing here plays on its own. Scroll position is wired straight to the timeline, so the ice melts as fast as you move and freezes the moment you stop. Scroll back up and it refreezes.

Why it holds together

The sequence is cut from two separately generated takes. Joining that kind of footage usually shows — exposure drifts, the subject jumps, and the cut announces itself. This one measures 0.80 on a frame-difference scale where an invisible seam sits around 2.3, so the join reads as a single continuous shot.

Getting there meant throwing away a third take entirely. It covered the same stretch of melt at a different exposure, which produced both a visible pop at the cut and roughly three seconds where almost nothing changed on screen.

The sequence

  • 0.0sThe logo sits in the dark, before anything happens.
  • 1.2sLight enters from above and the ice begins to give.
  • 4.8sThe numerals dissolve, leaving the word standing alone.
  • 6.9sCamera pushes through the lettering into black.

Sound follows the scroll

The audio is cut from the same two takes on the same frames, so it lands where the picture lands. It is rebuilt continuously as you scroll rather than played back — overlapping windows of the original recording, each faded in and out on a curve that sums to exactly the level of the one before it. Stop scrolling and the room goes quiet.

Where it ends

The last frame fades to true black and the page simply continues out of it — no cut, no divider, no change of colour. The film does not stop so much as open into the page you are reading.
